newsitem.title: UK: BoE's Davies encouraged by reaction to "Super SIB".
newsitem.headline: BoE's Davies encouraged by reaction to "Super SIB".

text.p: Deputy Bank of England Governor Howard Davies, soon to head up a new, all-embracing financial regulator, said on Wednesday he was encouraged by market reaction to the planned structure.
Davies pledged to guard against the new Securities and Investment Board, or "Super SIB" as it has been called, becoming too unwieldy.
"I have been quite encouraged, so far, by the market reaction to the proposed new structure," Davies told the Futures and Options Association International Derivatives Week conference in London.

"Warning notes have been sounded...about the need to avoid a lumbering, slow-moving bureaucracy and the need to ensure that regulation is appropriate for the type of market," Davies said, adding that he understood those concerns -- particularly the need to distinguish between wholesale and retail businesses.
"But, overall, I sense that we begin the task with some goodwill in the marketplace."

Last month, Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown announced he was stripping the Bank of England of its role in regulating Britain's banking sector and said a revamped SIB would oversee bank, insurance companies and securities houses.
Davies referred to a survey of Futures and Options Association members, conducted late last year.

"The strongest message to emerge...was the need for regulators to consult the market effectively on both structures and rules," he said. "I am certainly prepared to undertake here and now that we shall do so."

He said discussions with market participants needed to start right away, adding that he also took the point about the need for cost control on the one hand and a framework which promotes innovation on the other.
